# dtcloud_snapshot (Data Source)

Looks up one snapshot by id.

Use it to reference a snapshot Terraform did not take. Declaring such a snapshot as a resource would hand Terraform ownership of it, and a later destroy would delete the copy it was there to protect.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dtcloud_snapshot" "nightly" {
  id = var.snapshot_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) ID of the snapshot to look up.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the snapshot was taken, as the platform reports it. The API sends no timezone, and the value is passed through unchanged.
- `description` (String) Free-text description, as the platform reports it.
- `name` (String) Name of the snapshot.
- `progress` (String) How far the copy has got, as a percentage string such as `100%`. The only visible sign that a large snapshot is still being written.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project the snapshot belongs to.
- `size` (Number) Size in GB, inherited from the source volume. A snapshot cannot be resized; it is as large as the volume was when it was taken.
- `status` (String) Status reported by the platform. `available` is the only resting state.
- `storage_policy` (String) Name of the storage policy backing the snapshot, resolved from `volume_type_id`. Empty if the storage-policies endpoint could not be read.
- `updated_at` (String) When the snapshot's metadata last changed. Empty until it is first renamed or re-described.
- `volume_id` (String) ID of the volume the snapshot was taken from.
- `volume_type_id` (String) ID of the volume type backing the snapshot, as the snapshots endpoint reports it. `storage_policy` is the same thing by name.
